params.newsHook: Given that LLM models are engines of bullshit, here are the most important issues to address

opeds.headline: Stop Treating Stochastic Guesswork Like Oracle Wisdom
opeds.subtitle: Large language models are not oracles of the future. They are statistical guesswork engines, and we need to treat them like the leaky infrastructure they actually are.
opeds.body:
Harry Frankfurt taught us to spot a bullshitter a mile away. Unlike a liar, who knows the truth and goes to work hiding it, the bullshitter does not care about the truth at all. Truth is simply not a variable in his function. As jsnover points out in his recent analysis, large language models are not malicious liars. They are pure, unadulterated bullshit engines.

Yet the public debate remains trapped in a fantasy. Tech executives and doomers alike treat these probability calculators as if they were prophetic entities. They argue over whether the machine will save civilization or destroy it, completely ignoring what is actually happening in the math. The model takes a token, runs it through a stack of weights, and spits out a probability distribution over the next token. There is no truth register. There is no fact table. There is only a sampler.

When jsnover built his AI Rosetta Stone project at Harvard's Berkman Klein Center, he ran straight into this physical wall. The system kept hallucinating a sixteenth dialectic move, ignoring explicit prompt instructions to stop. No amount of polite talking to the prompt fixed it. Prompt engineering is a prayer circle for people who do not want to write code. It fails because it treats a stochastic inference engine like an attentive human assistant.

We need to grow up and put on our engineering pants. Every reliable digital system we rely on today is built on top of unreliable components. Internet Protocol drops packets. Spinning hard drives fail. Cosmic rays flip bits in memory. Engineers do not weep over this reality. They build guardrails, runtimes, and boundary checks.

That is why jsnover is entirely right to insist that model output must be treated as untrusted user input. You do not take raw strings from a stranger and execute them against your database. You validate the schema. You enforce strict boundaries. You write mini-fixers to catch the drift before it breaks the system. If commercial vendors locked operators out of internal telemetry, we have to force open the black box through mandated liability rules and rigorous runtime audits.

Let us stop pretending we are summoning a divine intelligence. We are operating a very large, very loud, and deeply leaky pipe of statistical guesswork. Treat it like infrastructure, or stop complaining when the basement floods.

opeds.rhetorical_meta: This piece uses a demystifying, materialist strategy to ground the abstract hype of AI into standard software engineering principles. By leaning on Frankfurt's theory of bullshit and concrete programming realities like schema validation, it strips away utopian and apocalyptic theater to expose corporate negligence.
